summary: POST /api/query trusts client sessionId without ownership check
description:
POST /api/query accepts a client-supplied `sessionId` and inserts the new query into that session without verifying it belongs to the authenticated user. A user can write queries into another user's session, polluting their history.

Fix options (any one):
- Pre-check: `SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` before INSERT; 404/403 if absent.
- Single-statement guard: fold the ownership check into the INSERT via a sub-select or CTE so the row only inserts when the session belongs to the user.
- Schema-level: tighten queries.session_id FK + add CHECK or trigger that asserts queries.user_id matches sessions.user_id.

Severity: HIGH — cross-user data integrity.
